messages:
maria.ng: Heads-up: I found a reproducible case where the Go SDK generator returns duplicate token chunks if auth refresh (token rotation) happens mid-stream. Minimal sampleapp + logs below. Repro on go-sdk @ master.

alex.p: Can you paste the sampleapp and the logs? Which SDK version exactly?

maria.ng: Quick client snippet (very small):

```go
ctx := context.Background()
req := sdk.GenerateRequest{ Model: \"open-llm/fastgen\", Prompt: \"...\" }
gen, err := client.Generate(ctx, req)
if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
for gen.Next() {
    tok := gen.Token()
    fmt.Print(tok)
}
if gen.Err() != nil { log.Println(\"gen error:\", gen.Err()) }
```

When the access token rotates (we test with a short-lived test token), the SDK reconnects the stream. After reconnect, the client sees the last ~2 tokens repeated, then resume. Logs show repeated sequence ids.

maria.ng: Paste of logfile around reconnect: 

```
2026-03-20T15:02:10Z auth: refresh started
2026-03-20T15:02:11Z auth: refresh succeeded, new exp=2026-03-20T15:07:10Z
2026-03-20T15:02:11Z stream: reconnecting to /generate (reason=auth-refresh)
2026-03-20T15:02:11Z stream: resumed from seq=42
2026-03-20T15:02:11Z stream: emitting seq=41 token=\"the\"
2026-03-20T15:02:11Z stream: emitting seq=42 token=\"quick\"
2026-03-20T15:02:11Z stream: emitting seq=43 token=\"brown\"
```

You can see seq=41/42 repeated after resume.

alex.p: Huh. Do we reconstruct the request state on reconnect? Is the server doing replay or is the client re-sending a window?

kevin.h: We glanced at this in eng-runtime a while back. If the client reconnects naively it can re-request from last acked offset; if the server uses inclusive indexes you can get overlap. Two quick angles: server should accept an exclusive resume offset, or client should provide a resume token that the server understands.

maria.ng: Right. The current SDK reconnect logic tries to be helpful: it asks server to resume from last seen seq. But it doesn't coordinate whether that seq was already delivered to the app layer. Hence the duplicates.

sophie.t: Short-term workaround: scrub duplicates at the app layer (drop tokens with seq <= lastSeen). But that's painful for users and duplicate detection needs seq metadata which our generator.Token() currently doesn't expose (it just returns bytes).

alex.p: Can we add seq metadata to the generator API? e.g., `gen.Token() (tok string, seq int64)`? That will make dedupe easier.

kevin.h: We could, but that leaks server internals. Better long-term: SDK returns a resume token opaque string (atomic) on initial open. On reconnect client sends `Resume-Token: <opaque>` and server resumes without overlapping. Also add option `WithResumeStrategy(ResumeExclusive|ResumeInclusive|Restart)` for backwards compatibility.

maria.ng: I sketched a tiny patch to return a resume token from the initial handshake and include an option to prefer server-exclusive resumes. Patch snippet: 

```diff
diff --git a/generate.go b/generate.go
@@
- func (c *Client) Generate(ctx context.Context, req GenerateRequest) (*Generator, error) {
+ func (c *Client) Generate(ctx context.Context, req GenerateRequest) (*Generator, error) {
     // existing init
+     // expose resumeToken from handshake -> gen.resumeToken
      ...
 }
@@
 type Generator struct {
     // existing fields
+    resumeToken string // opaque token from server handshake
 }
```

maria.ng: Repro steps I used: 1) run sampleapp with DEBUG=1; 2) issue a token rotation via our test auth server; 3) observe reconnect in logs; 4) compare emitted tokens around reconnect. I'll open a tiny repo showing the repro.

ci-bot: CI: test `go-sdk/generator` failed on `gen-stream-auth-reconnect_test` on linux/amd64  https://ci.redwood.example/build/12345 (flaky?)

alex.p: Good catch. Sophie / Kevin  do you want a short ADR or lean design doc before a PR? I can pair on the API naming.

sophie.t: Please yes. Key constraints:
- keep existing generator ergonomics (don't force callers to handle seq unless they opt-in)
- opt-in resume semantics so we don't change behaviors for existing users
- provide a clear migration path and sampleapp that shows dedupe and resume usage

kevin.h: I'll draft the server-side resume semantics we discussed (exclusive resume token) and wire up tests that fail when server incorrectly replays. That will make the CI deterministic.

maria.ng: I'll open the sampleapp repro + a WIP PR linking the design doc. Starting with opt-in `WithResumeToken()` and `Generator.ResumeToken()` to keep it additive.

alex.p: sgtm. Thanks for the debug and repro, @maria.ng. Helpful. :thumbsup:

maria.ng: Thanks all  ping me if you want to pair on the PR review or the sampleapp steps.
